Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • The provided evidence does not show .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, clearly malicious install-time setup.py logic, malicious PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects.
  • User-invoked CLI entry points such as console_scripts are not automatic execution evidence and are not treated as malicious indicators.
  • The pre-scan “encrypted-payload-primitive” hits in XML appear to be false positives from Quantum ESPRESSO crystallographic symmetry data (rotation, inversion, time_reversal), not execution paths or loader evidence.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: no evidence of broad collection of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, GitHub/PyPI/npm tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets.
  • Staging/exfiltration: no evidence of archiving/staging followed by upload, webhooks, raw IP endpoints, paste/drop services, or attacker-controlled C2 domains.
  • Persistence: no evidence of cron, systemd, launch agents, shell profile modification, startup registration, or background polling loops.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence of Kubernetes token use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, CI/CD token reuse, or GitHub Actions workflow injection.
  • Obfuscation/loader: no evidence of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal loaders, encrypted payloads, or downloader stubs. The XML inversion/rotation strings appear to be scientific computation data.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided evidence, there is no confirmed sign of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting, sudden dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch.
  • The observed URLs appear related to the project repository, documentation/library badges, GNU/FSF license text, and Quantum ESPRESSO XML namespaces/output data; there is no evidence they are attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoints.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input is limited to selected extracted files and partial text. Among the 120 total files, PNGs, pickle files (.pkl), and large data files were not fully validated from text evidence alone.
  • For a stronger distribution-integrity conclusion, compare the PyPI sdist against the upstream GitHub tag/commit, verify the provenance and necessity of included .pkl files, and review the full contents of pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and devtools/setup.py.
